dossier.summary: Juniper Payroll is payroll and tip-pooling software for restaurant groups with 5 to 50 locations. It connects to the main restaurant point-of-sale systems and pays staff weekly.
dossier.why_now: Hiring a head of growth, posted in October.

data.summary: Your homepage leads with the modern payroll platform for hospitality. The sketch leads with tip pooling and weekly pay for restaurant groups, which your How it works section already describes.

today.headline: The modern payroll platform for hospitality
today.sub: Juniper brings payroll, tips and scheduling together in one place so you can focus on running great restaurants.
today.section_body: Connect your point of sale, import your team, and run payroll in minutes. Tips are pooled and split by the rules you set, and every employee gets paid on time.

sketch.headline: Payroll and tip pooling for restaurant groups, paid out weekly
sketch.sub: Juniper runs payroll for groups with 5 to 50 locations, pools tips by the rules you set, and pays staff every week.
sketch.proof: Built for groups with 5 to 50 locations, connected to your point of sale
sketch.image: A manager closing out Friday tips on a phone in the back office
sketch.section_heading: From point of sale to payday in three steps
sketch.section_intro: What a payroll week looks like once Juniper is connected to the tills.

points.title: Connect the point of sale
points.text: Hours and tips come in from the tills at each location, so nothing is keyed in twice.

points.title: Set the tip rules
points.text: Pool and split tips by the rules you set once, and Juniper applies them every week.

points.title: Run payroll weekly
points.text: Every employee at every location is paid on time, every week.

notes.note: Names the two things the product does and the buyer it is for. The modern payroll platform could sit on a competitor's site unchanged.
The 5 to 50 locations line tells a group with 12 restaurants in one read that this is sized for them.
A sample payroll shows the product doing the work. Get started asks for a sign-up before the reader knows what it does.
Frames the section as a week in the life, so an operations lead reads it as their own routine.
The three steps keep your order and get a line each on what happens at the till, in the rules and on payday.
